user.title: Collect a report from an access point
user.description:
For an access point that isn't supported yet: Home Assistant reads it once and keeps a redacted report, which you then download with Download diagnostics and attach to a "New access point model" issue. Nothing is added to your setup, and passwords, communities and keys are used for this collection only and not stored.

How can Home Assistant read this access point?

menu_options.ssh: SSH console (login with username and password)

ssh.title: Collect a report over SSH
ssh.description: Home Assistant logs in, runs the built-in display commands and validates extra commands, then keeps a redacted report.

data_description.profile: Generic tries common show/get commands. Choose a vendor list if yours is there.
data_description.commands: One command per line that lists the connected clients, e.g. show, get or display commands, iw dev wlan0 station dump, iwinfo wlan0 assoclist, wlanconfig ath0 list, wl assoclist, read-only ubus calls or a MikroTik print command. Shell chaining, redirection and expansion are refused; other commands are skipped.
data_description.legacy_ssh: Turn on if the connection fails with an algorithm error (older access points, e.g. D-Link DAP).

snmp_v2c.title: Collect a report over SNMP v2c
snmp_v2c.description: Home Assistant reads the access point's system details, its vendor's own tables and the standard wireless tables, and lists the tables that look like client tables. Values outside those are shown only as their length. Use a read-only community: v2c sends it unencrypted over your network.

snmp_v3.title: Collect a report over SNMP v3
snmp_v3.description: Home Assistant reads the access point's system details, its vendor's own tables and the standard wireless tables, and lists the tables that look like client tables. Values outside those are shown only as their length.

data_description.priv_key: Leave empty to use the authentication key.

progress.collecting:
Collecting a report from {host}. This takes up to {duration}.

You can close this window: the collection continues. Its result (the report, or why it failed) then appears in Download diagnostics: Settings → Devices & services → Wi-Fi Association Presence → the menu (⋮) on the Wi-Fi association presence row → Download diagnostics.

error.collection_in_progress: Another access point report is still being collected. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
error.invalid_auth: The access point rejected the username or password.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the access point over SSH. Check the address, port and that SSH is enabled.
error.legacy_ssh: The access point only offers old SSH algorithms. Turn on "Allow old SSH algorithms" and try again.
error.invalid_snmp_auth: The access point rejected the SNMPv3 user, keys or algorithms.
error.snmp_no_answer: No SNMP answer. Check the address and port, the community (v2c) or user (v3), and that SNMP is enabled on the access point.
error.timeout: The access point did not finish answering in time.
error.unknown: Unexpected error, see the Home Assistant log.

abort.report_ready:
**Report collected in {elapsed}.**

⚠️ **Read the whole report before you submit it.** Automatic redaction removes MAC, IP and email addresses, key-like strings and the password, community or keys you typed, but it can't recognise everything: a Wi-Fi passphrase, names, locations or serial numbers can look like ordinary text. Replace anything you don't want public by hand. Issues on GitHub are public.

To download it, open the [Wi-Fi Association Presence page]({integration_url}), then the menu (⋮) on the **Wi-Fi association presence** row at the top, and choose **Download diagnostics**. The report is the `access_point_report` part of that file.

Later you find it the same way: Settings → Devices & services → Wi-Fi Association Presence → ⋮ → Download diagnostics. It is kept until Home Assistant restarts or you collect another report.

The file also contains Home Assistant's usual diagnostics details (your Home Assistant version and the list of custom integrations). Once you have read it, attach it to a [New access point model]({issue_url}) issue.
